rewrite.prompt:
RSW_SmogMoth lights up like a floodlight

The smog moth's description says it glows faintly, but in game it is brighter than a standing lamp. Its CompProperties_Glower in SWBestiary (Defs/BiomesTeamPort/ThingDefs_Races/RSW_BiomesTeamPort_Races.xml, around line 6370) is empty, so the engine fills in its defaults: glow radius 14 and colour 369/369/369, about 1.45x white.

RSW_Glowtail, in the same file, has a smaller version of the same problem: its glower sets a radius but no colour, so it also shines 1.45x white.

Repro: TheRot already has a rule for this. glower_findings() in src/RimMandrake/TheRot/Tools/selftest_rot_glowers.py flags any glower that is missing glowRadius or glowColor. Run it over SWBestiary's defs and both creatures are reported.

Expected: all of SWBestiary's glower comps state their own glowRadius and glowColor. The smog moth should get a small, faint glow in a colour that suits it, and the glowtail should get a colour. defNames stay as they are.
rewrite.criteria: All glower comps (CompProperties_Glower) in src/RimStarWars/SWBestiary/Defs set both glowRadius and glowColor, so TheRot's glower_findings() reports nothing there. RSW_SmogMoth's glow is small and faint; RSW_Glowtail has a colour. No defName changes.

rewrite.prompt:
launch_ready: an exception inside run() loses the verdict, the receipt and the steps already taken

src/RimMandrake/bridgetools/launch_ready.py run() reports every outcome as a verdict (READY, KILL_FAILED, LAUNCH_NO_PROCESS and so on) and exit_code() maps it to the process exit code. But if anything inside run() raises, for example a powershell or taskkill call that hangs and raises subprocess.TimeoutExpired after the game was launched, the exception escapes as a traceback. There is no verdict line and no receipt, and the record of what was already done (a kill, a launch) is lost, so the caller cannot tell whether a game is now running.

Repro: in the selftest's fake environment, make the process listing raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired once the launch has happened, then call run(). It raises instead of returning a result.

Expected: run() never raises. Any exception becomes a new verdict, LAUNCHER_ERROR, returned like the other verdicts. Its why text names the exception and lists the steps taken so far (so a run that got as far as the launch says "launched"). exit_code() for it is 1, an ordinary failure. It is never READY and is not retried, since the game may be up.
rewrite.criteria: When anything inside launch_ready.run() raises (including subprocess.TimeoutExpired after the launch), run() returns a result with verdict LAUNCHER_ERROR instead of raising; its why names the exception and lists the steps already taken (e.g. "launched"); exit_code() returns 1 for it.

rewrite.prompt:
enact: rows clicked on an older sheet build get installed unverified when a catch row comes first

art/enact.py build_plan(decisions, holds, ..., stale=...) takes a stale argument: rows whose letters were clicked before the sheet's columns were rebuilt. Each such row should never be installed; it should appear in the plan's conflicts as "<row>: letter(s) <letters> were clicked before the sheet's columns were rebuilt ..." so the owner re-confirms it on the current sheet.

That works on its own, but not when the decisions file also has a catch row (a row like RM_XCatch, the catch item of creature RM_X) marked redo, placed before the stale row. Then the stale row is installed as if it had been verified, with no conflict.

Repro: take a decisions document that build_plan handles correctly with stale={"RM_Foo": ["B"]} (RM_Foo is reported as a conflict). Add a decision {"decision": "redo"} for a catch row such as RM_RedoCatch ahead of the existing decisions and call build_plan again with the same stale argument. RM_Foo now shows up in the plan's install list and no longer in conflicts.

Expected: a stale row is always a conflict and never installed, whatever other rows the decisions file holds and in whatever order.
rewrite.criteria: build_plan(..., stale={row: letters}) reports every stale row as a "<row>: letter(s) ..." conflict and never installs it, also when a catch row marked redo comes before it in the decisions file.

The patch file stays a list of PatchOperationRemove operations.

rewrite.prompt:
--compose biomes plan calls a committed source delete a hand edit

With deploy_custom_mods.py --compose biomes, the composed mod's game copy lays each source folder out under Biomes/<key>/ (the compose manifest's entries map a key to a source folder under the tier's source dir, e.g. key Warscar -> source Scarlands). When a file is deleted in a commit in the source folder, the plan should call its leftover game copy a stale deploy. Instead the plan labels it a game-only hand edit ('kept, --pull'), because the repo-deleted test is skipped for the composed target: it cannot map the game-side Biomes/<key>/... path back to a source path. Seen live: Biomes/Warscar/.../RM_TetchikJar.xml, deleted in d28a529cff from Scarlands/.

Repro: in a git repo, commit Scarlands/Defs/Jar.xml and Scarlands/Defs/Keep.xml under the biomes tier source dir, then git rm Jar.xml and commit. With a manifest whose entries include {"key": "Warscar", "source": "Scarlands"}, the game-only file Biomes/Warscar/Defs/Jar.xml is reported as a hand edit.

Expected: add a helper deploy_custom_mods.composed_repo_deleted(gone, manifest) -> set. gone is a list of game-only relative paths in the composed mod and manifest is the compose manifest dict (with its "entries" list of {key, source, ...}). It returns the subset of gone that maps through an entry (Biomes/<key>/<rest> -> <tier source dir>/<source>/<rest>, relative to SRC_ROOT) to a file that the source folder's git history tracked and later deleted. A game-only file the repo never tracked (a real hand edit) is not in the result, a path outside every entry (e.g. About/About.xml) is not in the result, and an empty list gives an empty set. The compose plan uses it so such files read as repo deletions.
rewrite.criteria: deploy_custom_mods.composed_repo_deleted(gone, manifest) returns a set holding Biomes/<key>/... paths whose source file (via the manifest entry's source folder) was tracked and deleted in git, and excludes never-tracked hand edits and paths outside any entry; an empty gone gives set().

rewrite.prompt:
enact apply: one facing refused at install still lands its siblings (mixed sets)

The plan already refuses a pick whole when one of its facings is refused (an owner-kept live file or a shared-file clash). At apply time, though, art/enact.py installs each facing on its own: when L.install raises L.Refused for one facing, the pick's other facings still install. The creature is then drawn from two sets, which is exactly the picture the plan-side refusal exists to prevent. Two related problems:
- a rebind group is rebound when any one of its installs succeeds, so a def can be pointed at a path whose other facing never landed;
- a folder's shed retires (retires with no replaced_by) are gated on any install on the row, so a ticked variant that installs sheds the folder even when the folder pick itself failed.

Repro: run enact(decisions, apply=True, no_deploy=True) with build_plan returning a plan that has a two-facing pick for RM_A letter B (Things/A_east.png carrying a rebind, and Things/A_north.png), plus on row RM_F a variant V install and a folder pick P install, and a retire row for RM_F's old file whose "gate" key lists the letters it depends on, here "gate": ["P"]. Make L.install raise L.Refused for A_north.png and for P's file. Today A_east.png lands, its rebind is made, and RM_F's old file is retired.

Expected:
- A pick (row, letter) lands whole or not at all: if any of its installs is refused, none of its facings is installed, not even for a moment (an install-then-undo still leaves the live mod with a mixed set while it runs, and an undo can itself fail). L.install raises L.Refused on a dry run as well, so a refusal can be known before anything is written. The refusal is listed in the result's conflicts, naming the refused file (A_north.png).
- A rebind is made only when every install of its group landed.
- A retire row with a "gate" list is applied only when a pick of a letter it lists landed on that row; installs of other letters on the row do not count. Here RM_F's variant V still lands, but the old folder file is not retired because P, the only gated letter, failed.
rewrite.criteria: In enact(..., apply=True), a pick with one L.Refused facing installs none of its facings (none is ever installed, not even and then undone) and its refusal is listed in conflicts naming the file; no rebind is made for a half-landed group; a retire row with "gate": [letters] is skipped when no pick of a listed letter landed, while other picks on the row still install.

rewrite.prompt:
enact: a schema-1 keyed pick installs at a lane its letter has since left; ruled_snapshot trusts git order

In art/enact.py build_plan, a schema-1 pick keyed to a lane (picks{<lane>: <letter>}) goes straight to that lane. A pick derived from a decision gets two guards that a keyed pick does not: it is refused when the letter moved between two lanes that both exist today, and when the letter does not show the same pictures on the clicked sheet as on today's sheet. So a keyed letter that a rebuild re-filed under another existing lane still installs at the old keyed lane: a wrong texture at a lane path where that letter's pictures no longer belong. Real cases: greentide RSW_Hawkbat G, keyed to the adult flying lane _flip:swanimals/Hawkbat/Hawkbat_Flying_ and filed under Hawkbat_j_Flying_ today (both lanes exist); RSW_PekoPeko E, keyed to f_Flying_ and filed under m_Flying_ today. 25 of 173 keyed picks are in a different lane today. No real install happens yet, only because each case is keep-blocked or refused elsewhere.

Repro (selftest_enact_stale_lane case 4's setup, an adult lane AD and a young lane, both existing today, Y filed under young today): history [older({A: AD, B: AD, C: AD, Y: AD})], plan {"schema": None, "picks": {AD: "Y"}}: Y installs at the AD path.

Expected: a keyed pick gets the same guards as a decision pick: Y is named as refused in conflicts, with no install of Y at either lane, and Y is not in lane_resolved. The same refusal applies when Y is still filed under AD but shows different pictures. Picks that are all live keep their exemption.

Second defect, same area: ruled_snapshot(path, current, click) walks the sheet's git revisions in git log order and stops at the first one built at or before the click. Commits from different clones can land out of build order, so it can pick an older build than the newest one at or before the click. Expected: it reads the whole bounded window (SNAP_REV_MAX revisions) and takes the newest build at or before the click. A revision in that window that cannot be read (not valid JSON, so its build time is unknown) could be that build, so then there is no answer: None, with the reason saying "unreadable" and naming the revision by at least the first 10 characters of its sha, never an older copy standing in for it. With a window that holds only readable revisions, the newest qualifying build is returned. Bounding, timeouts and snapshots outside the repository keep their current behaviour (a reason, never a crash).

Third defect, back in build_plan: a pick whose lane on the sheet he clicked on was a DONOR's lane (a path where nothing of ours ships, such as a vanilla placeholder texPath) is routed to today's lane without any proof. Expected: such a pick, schema 1 (decision or keyed) and a schema-2 slot keyed by the donor lane alike, is refused by name in conflicts ("<row>: pick <letter> ...refused...", or "<row>: slot <lane> pick <letter> ...refused..." for a slot) and installed nowhere, unless the repoint is proved. It is proved only when all of these hold: on the sheet he clicked on, the row's graphic (res) was the donor lane; today no def of the row names the donor lane and one names today's lane, which is where today's sheet files the letter; today's lane was not already a lane of the clicked sheet; and the letter shows the same pictures on both sheets. A proved pick installs at today's lane (never under the donor path) with no conflict for that row, and this holds even when the donor lane is still a column of today's row. If the letter showed other pictures on the clicked sheet, or the clicked sheet's res was not the donor lane, it is refused.
rewrite.criteria: Keyed schema-1 picks are refused (named in conflicts, not installed, not in lane_resolved) when the letter moved between two existing lanes or shows different pictures; ruled_snapshot scans the whole bounded window for the newest build at or before the click, and returns None with a reason naming at least the first 10 characters of the unreadable revision's sha and saying 'unreadable' when an unreadable revision in the window could be that build. A pick on a donor lane (nothing of ours ships there) is refused by name and installed nowhere unless the repoint is proved (clicked sheet's res was the donor lane, today a row def names today's lane and none the donor, today's lane was not a lane of the clicked sheet, same pictures); a proved one installs at today's lane only, even if the donor lane is still a column today.

rewrite.prompt:
Close evidence can be credited for tests that never ran or files they never covered (six defects)

A review of the close-evidence chain (run_selftests.py, close_evidence.py, arbiter_tiers.py) found six ways evidence over-claims:
1. run_selftests runs every test child with cwd set to the instrument clone, not the checkout being tested, so a test in another checkout (special invocations included) runs against the wrong tree.
2. A cached PASS (the test did not run this time) is written as fresh, covered PASS evidence.
3. A winbuild PASS covers the whole source folder, crediting unrelated src files.
4. Declared csproj covers ignore Compile Remove / Exclude and conditions.
5. Records are deduplicated by their mac, so a genuine FAIL -> PASS -> FAIL written in the same second by the same process collapses and an earlier result can win.
6. An abbreviated sha that is ambiguous in one clone fails open.

Expected:
1. A test runs with cwd = the checkout it belongs to; special invocations are looked up and built for that checkout; a test in the instrument clone still runs from there.
2. A cached PASS is never fresh close evidence: it is not among the record's paths and nothing it declares is covered. The record names the cached tests in detail.not_run_cached (a list of their repo paths). A run in which every test was a cache hit writes no record, and lookup finds no evidence for a cache hit.
3. A winbuild PASS covers the csproj and the compile items listed in its own .srchash stamp whose hashes match the clone, nothing else. A build with no stamp covers only its csproj. An old or forged "covers FOLDER" entry covers nothing beneath it, and any tool's covers entry beyond its paths matches only as itself, while a path a non-build tool was pointed at still covers as a folder.
4. Declared csproj covers honour Compile Remove and Exclude (case-insensitive, ';'-separated lists, so OLD/** does not match OLD2/). Conditions on compile items, Imports, properties, legacy (non-SDK) projects and a Directory.Build file that touches Compile all fail closed: the csproj itself only. A non-SDK project gets no default **/*.cs. A Condition on a Reference or unrelated property does not close the project.
5. Every record carries its own field nonce: a fresh random string of at least 32 characters, covered by the mac. FAIL -> PASS -> FAIL in the same second stays three records and the last FAIL decides; a replayed line with the same mac is still deduped.
